label: Lyrics on two lines
notes: A long lyric line breaks in two at a word edge, with the robot a little higher, so the whole line shows.
A rest of two bars or more shows a bar filling where the words go, like a karaoke video; for its last two half notes the next line's words come back.

label: Song import and sync
notes: Sync saves songs to their slots reliably.

label: Public Release Candidate
notes: Sings: import a karaoke (.kar) or MIDI song, or type a line on the FM-1 and play its notes on the keys; the voice is the 386 DX Engine, sung to your pitches and lengths.
Typing a line: the FM-1 counts its syllables, then you play a key for each one. Lines can be reordered, moved, and copied by reference, so a chorus is written once.
The face is the voice: it hops with the pitch, wobbles with vibrato, opens its mouth with the sound, and wears ^ ^ eyes on high notes and – – eyes on low ones.
Four tracks: Voice, Keys, Bass and Drums, with sound lists, a step sequencer (hold a step to edit it), live recording, tempo, and Voice settings you can change mid-song.
Sixteen punch-in effects under your fingers, several at once. The key lights show where you are (every fourth key) and blink the last one used.
Eight song slots with LOAD, SAVE TO, NEW SONG and RENAME SONG. Greensleeves is in S1 the first time it starts, and you can write over it.
This page installs and updates 386DX itself, puts songs into the slots, downloads or deletes them (queue the changes, then Sync), and runs the firmware in the browser.
Thirteen public-domain standards come with the page, ready to put in a slot.
